literal: Peacock feather-loaded cart even, axle will break, those goods abundantly having increased if loaded.
translation: Even a cart loaded with light peacock feathers will have its axle break, if those goods are loaded in too great an excess.
modern: மென்மையான மயில் இறகுகளை ஏற்றிய வண்டியாக இருந்தாலும், அந்தப் பொருளை அளவுக்கு அதிகமாக ஏற்றினால் அதன் அச்சு முறிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid metaphor to warn against underestimating the cumulative weight of small things. Peacock feathers ('பீலி') are extremely light, but if a cart ('சாகாடு') is overloaded with them, its axle ('அச்சு') will still break. In the context of knowing one's strength, it teaches that taking on too many small, seemingly easy tasks or facing too many weak enemies at once can lead to one's downfall.
